A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their complete main texts, Algorithm 1, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical regret bounds and proofs, with no original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis results in the main text or appendices.

after.justification: v2 likewise contains theoretical analysis and proofs, without original empirical results in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: The written initialization changes from uniform probability on an undefined set A_c, with zero elsewhere, to 1/K for every arm (v1 Section 3.1; v2 Section 3.2). This is a limited specification correction; Algorithm 1's epoch structure, FTRL updates, rejection sampling, and loss estimation are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. Bidding and sleeping bandits remain motivating applications.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Discussions of earlier algorithms concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Revised theoretical parameter choices do not constitute changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version includes ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. Both appendices contain mathematical analysis.

E5.justification: No empirical uncertainty estimates, repeated runs, or significance tests appear in either version. The revised failure-probability guarantee is theoretical.

E6.justification: Neither version reports experimental scores, rankings, or qualitative evaluation findings. Changes to mathematical regret guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix B.5 introduce confidence-dependent tuning and an explicit 1-delta guarantee, replacing v1's final probability bound of 1-1/(KT)-8delta. B.5 changes the stated rate from ~Theta(sqrt(KT) log(1/delta)) to ~O(sqrt(KT log(1/delta))) and adds probability rescaling. The underlying lemmas and most derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: a near-optimal high-probability analysis of Schneider and Zimmert's existing algorithm for adversarial losses and unknown i.i.d. context distributions.

C2.justification: A new Appendix B.2 footnote explains why the proof uses Bias5_e F_e instead of Bias5_e G: the global event G need not be conditionally independent of the bias. v1 already used F_e but lacked this explanation.

D1.justification: The parameter prescription changes from iota=2 log(8KT) to iota=2 log(8KT/delta), with corresponding confidence-dependent choices of L, gamma, and eta. v2 also makes the uniform initialization explicit.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work survey are retained. However, the new Appendix B.2 footnote specifically criticizes a conditional-independence argument in Schneider and Zimmert (2023), adding a substantive distinction from the prior analysis.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: v2 introduces an early Technical Overview and informal theorem, separates the problem statement and algorithm exposition, and divides the analysis into three named subsections. Material from v1's Preliminaries and Main Analysis is redistributed with rewritten transitions and additional explanations.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is relocated, the formal theorem gains a separate displayed regret bound, and added headings and footnotes change page composition. The overall visual style remains stable, with no new figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision through explicit confidence-dependent tuning and the final 1-delta probability statement in Theorem 1 and Appendix B.5. The new dependence explanation and reorganized technical overview make the existing argument easier to assess. These are useful, limited gains within essentially the same theoretical analysis.
